EVALUATION CRITERIA: Usually not-applicable for unit tests unless explicit timing/security tests are present; presence of @Test(timeout=...) indicates a timing consideration.
DECISION RULES: The test method is annotated with @Test(timeout = 4000), an explicit timeout-based assertion; therefore it demonstrates a performance-related constraint.
VERDICT: compliant — the explicit timeout present in the test method satisfies the practice's detection criteria.

PRINCIPLE: Test names should describe scenario and expected outcome.
RATIONALE: Descriptive names make tests self-documenting.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if names follow methodName_scenario_expectedForm or BDD patterns; non-compliant if generic names like test1/test7.
DECISION RULES: The method is named 'test7', which is generic and does not describe the scenario or expected result.
VERDICT: non-compliant — method name is generic and does not convey purpose.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Generated tests should be minimal and intention-revealing.
RATIONALE: Heavily generated tests are verbose and less maintainable.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Non-compliant when auto-generated markers, repetitive names (test0/test1/test7) or comments like 'Auto-generated' appear.
DECISION RULES: The class includes EvoSuite artifacts (EvoRunner, EvoRunnerParameters, MaxMin3_ESTest_scaffolding, and a test named 'test7'), which are indicators of heavy test generation.
VERDICT: non-compliant — clear signs of autogenerated test patterns are present (EvoSuite runner and generic test naming).

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Tests should show clear design intent (Given-When-Then, TDD/BDD naming) and cover prioritized scenarios.
RATIONALE: Thoughtful design yields better coverage and maintainability.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant when tests contain Given-When-Then comments or BDD naming, or when multiple scenarios (happy+edge+error) are present.
DECISION RULES: The class comment claims some refactoring, but the single test method contains no Given-When-Then structure and only a trivial constructor invocation; comprehensive scenario coverage is absent.
VERDICT: non-compliant — test methods do not exhibit clear prioritized design or multiple scenario coverage.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Tests should rely on public APIs and avoid implementation details.
RATIONALE: Behavior-focused tests are less brittle.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Non-compliant if reflection or checking private fields; compliant when tests call public methods only.
DECISION RULES: The test only invokes the public constructor; there is no reflection or access to internals.
VERDICT: compliant — test interacts via public API (constructor) and does not rely on internal implementation details.

PRINCIPLE: Use specific assertions and include descriptive messages when helpful.
RATIONALE: Clear, specific assertions ease diagnosis and detect subtle faults.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if assertions are specific (assertEquals/assertThat) and many include messages; non-compliant if only generic assertions or none.
DECISION RULES: The test contains no assertions at all; therefore it fails to use assertions adequately.
VERDICT: non-compliant — absence of assertions means the test won't detect functional regressions.

PRINCIPLE: Comments should explain 'why' and not clutter obvious code; avoid commented-out code.
RATIONALE: Excessive or stale comments reduce clarity.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Non-compliant if commented-out code or >50% lines are comments; compliant if code is clean with minimal useful comments.
DECISION RULES: No commented-out code or excessive comments are present in the method; class-level Javadoc is useful.
VERDICT: compliant — the code is concise and there are no distracting commented-out blocks.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should avoid randomness, time, sleeps, and external dependencies without mocking.
RATIONALE: Deterministic tests avoid flakiness.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Non-compliant if Random(), System.currentTimeMillis(), Thread.sleep(), or external dependencies are used without mocks.
DECISION RULES: The test contains none of these non-deterministic constructs; it only constructs an object.
VERDICT: compliant — no sources of non-determinism are present in the visible method.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Tests should avoid modifying shared state or persistent side effects.
RATIONALE: Side effects cause test interdependencies and flakiness.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if tests use only local variables and perform no external persistence or static modifications.
DECISION RULES: The test only creates a local object and performs no file/database/static modifications and no cleanup is required.
VERDICT: compliant — no side effects or persisted state changes are present in the method.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Use @Tag/@Category to classify tests for selective execution.
RATIONALE: Labels help run subsets of tests in CI.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant when @Tag/@Category annotations are present and meaningful.
DECISION RULES: The class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class), which is meaningful class-level categorization.
VERDICT: compliant — category annotation is present and appropriate for unit tests.
